The use of a shell script ('bash ./install') can be even more dangerous as it can run any shell commands, potentially leading to system compromise or data exfiltration. There is no indication of legitimate build or setup rationale for this preinstall script, increasing suspicion. Unlike the known malicious patterns, this code does not execute arbitrary shell commands, does not spawn detached or hidden processes for persistence, nor does it automatically execute external payloads on import. The use of spawn with customFds is for redirecting stdio streams for testing, not for evasion or stealth. There is no evidence of obfuscation, command injection, or unauthorized system manipulation. The code is clearly structured as test helpers and test cases, indicating a benign intent.
